import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates (correlated pairs with |r| >= 0.6)
    correlated_pairs = [
        ('EFC4L', 'OPTP7'), ('OPTP7', 'IYZV11A'), ('EFC4L', 'IYZV11A'),
        ('OPTP7', 'KFDN5L'), ('OPTP7', 'RLQO14'), ('EFC4L', 'KFDN5L'),
        ('AAV13', 'OPTP7'), ('IYZV11A', 'KFDN5L'), ('OPTP7', 'MGU16L'),
        ('BKTD13', 'GXWZ2L'), ('XQBG6', 'OPTP7'), ('RLQO14', 'KFDN5L'),
        ('OPTP7', 'AUKX11P'), ('ERS6', 'OPTP7'), ('AAV13', 'IYZV11A'),
        ('EFC4L', 'AAV13'), ('ERS6', 'IYZV11A'), ('KFDN5L', 'MGU16L'),
        ('XQBG6', 'KFDN5L'), ('OPTP7', 'BKTD13')
    ]
    
    # Keep only one feature from each highly correlated pair
    keep_ids = set(feats.ids)
    for a, b in correlated_pairs:
        if a in keep_ids and b in keep_ids:
            # Prefer the one with higher effect size
            idx_a = feats.column(a)
            idx_b = feats.column(b)
            effect_a = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, idx_a]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, idx_a])
            effect_b = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, idx_b]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, idx_b])
            if abs(effect_a) >= abs(effect_b):
                keep_ids.remove(b)
            else:
                keep_ids.remove(a)
    
    # Filter features to only those we're keeping
    keep_indices = [feats.column(fid) for fid in keep_ids]
    filtered_ids = tuple(feat_id for feat_id in feats.ids if feat_id in keep_ids)
    
    # Compute effect sizes and select top candidates
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        effect = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, idx]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, idx])
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, idx], feats.x[feats.y==0, idx])
        effects.append((abs(effect), abs(t_stat), fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size and t-statistic
    effects.sort(reverse=True)
    selected_ids = [fid for _, _, fid in effects[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Check if any mechanism exists using logistic regression
    if len(selected_ids) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build model with selected features
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_ids]]
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
    
    # Fit logistic regression to get coefficients
    clf = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', random_state=42)
    clf.fit(X_scaled, feats.y)
    
    # Get feature weights
    weights = dict(zip(selected_ids, clf.coef_[0]))
    
    # Select drivers based on coefficient magnitude
    sorted_drivers = sorted(weights.keys(), key=lambda k: abs(weights[k]), reverse=True)
    drivers = tuple(sorted_drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Include all selected features in columns
    columns = selected_ids
    
    # No products needed for this simple case
    products = ()
    
    # Return the design
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=weights)
